full_judgment:
18. Mr. Hasib next contends at a contempt proceeding is like a criminal proceeding and the alleged contemner stands in the position of an accused who must be presumed to be innocent. This leads to the question of burden of proof in a contempt proceeding. A contempt proceeding is neither a criminal proceeding nor a civil proceeding but it has got the elements of both the proceedings and, as such, it is a class by it self. This question was considered on a previous occasion by a Division Bench of this Court in the case the State Vs. Maulana A.R. Tarkabagish, 10 DLR 568. It was held: 

 In a contempt case the alleged contemner may swear affidavit and depose as a witness, whereas in a criminal case the accused is not required to do so. But the onus of proof in a contempt proceedings lies on the person bringing the allegation and in the case of doubt the benefit must go to the opposite party, the alleged contemner.
